title: Wildlife & Nature Escapes Near Delhi
content:
Wildlife & Nature Escapes Near Delhi

Delhi’s fast-paced life calls for a refreshing break amidst greenery and wildlife. Luckily, nature lovers and wildlife enthusiasts have plenty of weekend getaways nearby — from national parks and bird sanctuaries to serene lakes and forested retreats. Whether you’re chasing the roar of the tiger, the flutter of migratory birds, or just peace among the hills, these wildlife and nature escapes promise an unforgettable weekend.

1. Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand)

Distance: 250 km (6 hours drive)
Best Time to Visit: November to June
Famous For: Tigers, elephants, jeep safaris, and lush forests

How to Reach Jim Corbett from Delhi (Short Version):

  • By Road: 250 km, 5-6 hours via NH9/Ghaziabad → Hapur → Ramnagar.
  • By Train: Delhi - Ramnagar (~10 km from park), then taxi to hotel or gate.
  • By Bus: State or private Volvo buses to Ramnagar, then taxi to park.
  • By Air: Pantnagar Airport (~75 km), then taxi to Corbett.

Tip: Book safari tickets online in advance for hassle-free entry.

3-Day Itinerary:

Day 1: Delhi - Jim Cobrbett → Evening nature walk along the Kosi River.
Day 2: Morning jeep safari → visit the Corbett Museum.
Day 3: Optional early safari or visit Garjia Devi Temple → returning to Delhi. Click here for detailed program

2. Ranthambore National Park (Rajasthan)

Distance (Delhi - Ranthambore) : 400 km (7-8 hours drive)
Best Time to Visit: October to April
Famous For: Bengal tigers, Ranthambore Fort, and rich flora-fauna diversity

How to Reach Ranthambore from Delhi (Short Version):

  • By Road: 400 km, 7–8 hours via NH48 → NH23, best for flexibility.
  • By Train: Delhi → Sawai Madhopur (5 km from park), trains like Shatabdi or Mewar Express.
  • By Bus: Rajasthan State Transport or private Volvo buses to Sawai Madhopur.
  • By Air: Jaipur Airport (170 km), then taxi or bus to Ranthambore.

4-Day Itinerary

Day 1: Delhi To Jaipur →Galta Ji Temple
Day 2: Jaipur excursion  (Amber Fort → City Palace → Local shopping in Bapu Bazaar)
Day 3: Jaipur to Ranthambore  →  Enjoy Safari 
Day 4: Ranthambore - Delhi Departure. Click here for detailed program

3. Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary (Keoladeo National Park, Rajasthan)

Distance: 220 km (4 hours drive)
Best Time to Visit: October to February (migratory season)
Famous For: Migratory birds like Siberian cranes, pelicans, and painted storks

3-Day Itinerary:

Day 1: Travel from Delhi to Bharatpur, check into hotel, evening bird-watching session.
Day 2: Early morning cycle or rickshaw safari in the sanctuary, visit Lohagarh Fort and Government Museum.
Day 3: Stop at Deeg Palace while returning to Delhi.

4. Sariska Tiger Reserve (Rajasthan)

Distance: 200 km (4.5 hours drive)
Best Time to Visit: October to June
Famous For: Tigers, leopards, and ancient temples within the reserve

3-Day Itinerary:

Day 1: Delhi → Drive to Sariska

Day 2: Early morning safari →visit Kankwari Fort → Pandupol Temple

Day 3: Returning to Delhi. Click her for detailed program 

5. Pangot & Nainital Region (Uttarakhand)

Distance: 320 km (7 hours drive)
Best Time to Visit: March to June & October to February
Famous For: Bird watching, forest walks, and scenic mountain views

3-Day Itinerary:

Day 1: Delhi to Nainital, check-in, explore the Mall Road and Naini Lake.

Day 2: Drive to Pangot for birdwatching trails and forest camping.

Day 3: Return to Nainital for boating or ropeway ride, then drive back to Delhi.

6. Sultanpur Bird Sanctuary (Haryana)

Distance: 45 km (1.5 hours drive)
Best Time to Visit: November to February
Famous For: Short day trip from Delhi, ideal for birdwatching and photography

3-Day Suggestion (for weekend extension):

Combine Sultanpur visit with Damdama Lake or Sohna Hot Springs nearby for a refreshing weekend escape.

How to Reach These Destinations

All these destinations are easily accessible by road from Delhi. Major ones like Jim Corbett, Bharatpur, and Ranthambore also have rail connectivity from Delhi and surrounding cities.

Travel Tips

  • Always pre-book safaris online to avoid last-minute unavailability.
  • Wear neutral-colored clothing and carry binoculars.
  • Avoid loud noise and respect the natural environment.
  • Carry sunscreen, a hat, and light snacks for safaris.

faqs.question: What are the best wildlife sanctuaries and nature escapes near Delhi?
faqs.answer: Some of the best wildlife and nature destinations near Delhi include Jim Corbett National Park, Ranthambore National Park, Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, Sariska Tiger Reserve, and Pangot in Uttarakhand.

faqs.question: How far is Jim Corbett National Park from Delhi, and how can I reach it?
faqs.answer: Jim Corbett is around 250 km from Delhi. You can reach it via a scenic road trip (around 6 hours) or take a train to Ramnagar, the nearest railway station.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit wildlife sanctuaries near Delhi?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit is from October to June, especially during winter and early summer, when animal sightings are frequent, and the weather is pleasant.

faqs.question: Do I need to book safari tickets in advance for places like Ranthambore or Corbett?
faqs.answer: Yes, it’s highly recommended to book safari tickets online in advance, as slots are limited and fill up quickly, especially during weekends and holidays.

faqs.question: Are there good nature resorts near Delhi for a peaceful stay?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are several nature resorts like Aahana Resort (Corbett), Sariska Tiger Camp, and Aranya Nature Resort (Bharatpur) that offer a relaxing experience amid greenery.
